title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: Bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Variance refers to the model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training set. Consider how removing a feature might simplify the model and affect these aspects.

title: Role of the 'veg' Column
text: The 'veg' column represents the pounds of vegetables bought. Think about how this feature contributes to predicting the total bill and what happens when it's removed from the model.

hintAnswer: The model's bias increases because it loses information about the relationship between vegetables and the total bill.
title: Impact on Bias
text: What happens to the model's ability to capture the relationship between vegetables and the total bill if the 'veg' column is removed?
choices: The model's bias increases because it loses information about the relationship between vegetables and the total bill.
The model's bias decreases because it becomes simpler.
The model's bias remains the same.

hintAnswer: The model's variance decreases because it becomes less sensitive to fluctuations in the training data.
title: Impact on Variance
text: How does removing the 'veg' column affect the model's variance?
choices: The model's variance increases because it becomes more complex.
The model's variance decreases because it becomes less sensitive to fluctuations in the training data.
The model's variance remains the same.
